solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: See 11
Jumble sale refreshments

indicators.note: to jumble things is to mix them up, so the next word's letters are reordered

explanation.surface: The tea and drinks served at a church jumble sale.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumble sale is a British charity sale of second-hand goods; here 'Jumble' is the signal acting on 'sale'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beers are drinks, a kind of refreshment, so the plural fits the plural noun.

clue.text: Start again with cod roe and dash off?

indicators.note: cod as an adjective means mock or sham, so the word after it is a fake version, its letters rearranged

parts.note: to dash off a note is to write it quickly, to pen it

explanation.surface: A fishmonger or chef deciding to restart after cod roe has been hurried away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cod' looks like the fish but is the adjective meaning sham, signalling that 'roe' is rearranged to REO.
explanation.definitionFit: To open something again after a closure is to resume it, starting it once more.

clue.text: Trump perhaps providing funding initially for urban environment

parts.note: a trump is one example of a playing card
providing means on condition that, if

indicators.note: initially says take just the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Reads like a politician linking a Trump-style funding plan to the urban environment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' looks like the president but is a card game trump.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh capital is a city, so it is one example of an urban setting.

clue.text: 'Aida' Melba's key title role?

indicators.note: key here means central or at the core, so the letters sit within the quoted opera and the singer's name

explanation.surface: Asks whether Aida was Nellie Melba's key title role on the opera stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Nellie Melba was a famous Australian soprano who was made a Dame; the panto dame is the comic man-in-a-frock role in British pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both an honorific title held by Melba and a stock pantomime part, hence title and role.

clue.text: Stalked and arrested

definitions.meaning: having a stalk, as a flower or glass does
halted or checked, as a flow of blood is

explanation.surface: A crime report: someone followed a victim and was then taken in by police.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant with a stalk can be described this way, and the verb also means stopped or held back a flow.

clue.text: Elite grand family almost engaged in criminal activity

parts.note: G is the slang abbreviation for a grand, a thousand pounds
a litter is a family of young animals born together

indicators.note: almost says the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: British slang says someone up to no good is 'at it'

explanation.surface: An upper-crust family turns out to be mostly mixed up in crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims AT IT, British slang for being busy at wrongdoing, to ATI.
explanation.definitionFit: The glamorous celebrity set are a social elite, the fashionable smart crowd.

clue.text: Every trick in the book and right weaponry to crush resistance before upcoming riot

indicators.note: to crush something is to squeeze it, so the sword's letters close around what follows

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword, a weapon

indicators.note: before says the resistance symbol comes ahead of the next part

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: in a down clue upcoming means rising, so the word riot is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned round

explanation.surface: Police throw everything at a riot: rights, weapons, crushing all resistance before trouble breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' reads riot from the bottom of this down light; 'to crush' has the fencing sword squeeze the resistance symbol and the turned riot between its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's full stock of pieces or skills is their whole range of tricks.

clue.text: Thorny issue being less than quick swapping bridge partners

indicators.note: in bridge West partners East, so one compass letter is exchanged for its partner

parts.note: something less than quick is slow

explanation.surface: A prickly matter at the bridge table, play being slow while partners change seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thorny issue' looks like a tricky problem, but it is the fruit issuing from the blackthorn.
explanation.definitionFit: The blackthorn bush bears this small sour fruit, its offspring or issue.

clue.text: 'Casualty' episode missing opening page, but whoever the writer, it'll take off

definitions.text: whoever the writer, it'll take off

indicators.note: missing says a letter is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: Casualty is a BBC hospital drama, so an episode is an A and E programme

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A writer submits a Casualty script without its first page, but it will still be a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital's emergency department; 'missing opening page' drops the P from PROGRAMME.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an airmail letter form, so whoever writes one, the letter flies off by plane.

clue.text: 'Trade in' a Chambers anagram for 'perform a repulsive act'

indicators.note: the clue openly says the quoted words are to be rearranged, with Chambers playing the dictionary

explanation.surface: A mock dictionary entry, as if Chambers listed a jumble of trade-in letters under a disgusting deed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chambers' is the famous dictionary, but here it is just eight letters of fodder; 'repulsive' means driving back attackers, not disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Defenders who take up positions behind street obstacles are trying to repel, that is repulse, an attack.

clue.text: Barrier in slip road

definitions.meaning: something that deters or repels interest
a side road leading off a main road

explanation.surface: A crash barrier standing in a motorway slip road.
explanation.definitionFit: Something off-putting is an obstacle to liking, and a road branching from a highway is an exit lane.

clue.text: Classic pocket radio that derailed tubes?

definitions.meaning: the small portable radio set of the 1960s
the semiconductor device that ended the era of vacuum tubes, or valves

explanation.surface: A vintage pocket radio blamed for wrecking the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: The portable set took its name from the semiconductor part that superseded valves in electronics.

clue.text: To do with mixed reaction for play

parts.note: re means concerning, to do with

indicators.note: mixed says the next word's letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A critic describing a play's mixed reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a drama but is the noun meaning leisure.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure activity and amusement are play in the sense of fun pursued for its own sake.

clue.text: With end of cigarette dangling between fingertips Pacino is untameable

indicators.note: something dangling between fingers is held inside them, so the letter goes between the two tips

parts.note: the tips, or outer letters, of finger are F and R

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the next word

parts.note: Al Pacino, the American actor

explanation.surface: Al Pacino with a cigarette hanging from his fingers, a wild, untamed figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild animal that has gone back to nature is untamed and hard to domesticate.

clue.text: Excited following Queen release

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina
to give vent to feelings is to release them

explanation.surface: Royal fans thrilled after the Queen is released.
explanation.definitionFit: Passionate and intense are synonyms of the answer, much like excited or ardent.

clue.text: Terrific hubbub about scarf concealing decolletage

indicators.note: about here means around, so the two words hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: A fuss over a scarf worn to cover a revealing neckline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' looks like the signal, but it belongs to the definition; 'about' does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: This light triangular shawl was worn over the shoulders to cover a low neckline.

clue.text: Vouchsafe tide's somewhat polluted

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A grand way of saying the tide is a bit dirty.
explanation.definitionFit: Foul-smelling water is stinking, which goes with being contaminated.

clue.text: Pandemonium shaking off any that might have fallen in front

definitions.text: that might have fallen in front

indicators.note: shaking off says the letters of the next word are lost from the first

parts.note: pandemonium is chaos, lawless disorder

explanation.surface: Chaos at a scene where people may have fallen over in front.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ANY come out of ANARCHY one at a time; 'fallen' points to fallen arches, i.e. flat feet.
explanation.definitionFit: The curve under the foot can collapse, giving flat feet, and a gateway curve can stand in front of a building.

clue.text: One is wrapping good boomerangs for Christmas visitors

indicators.note: a boomerang comes back, so the whole is turned round
wrapping means going around, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: one person saying they are: I am

explanation.surface: Someone wrapping a good boomerang as a Christmas present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapping' and 'Christmas' suggest gifts, but 'wrapping' puts G inside IAM and 'boomerangs' turns IGAM round.
explanation.definitionFit: The wise men of the Nativity came bearing gifts, the original seasonal callers.

clue.text: Wise man had worked in backward parts of America

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other
backward says the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the United States, US, made of its states

indicators.note: worked means kneaded or reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sage who laboured in remote backwaters of America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns the country's initials round, and 'worked' scrambles had before 'in' sets it inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu holy man or ascetic is revered for spiritual wisdom.

clue.text: Roll a must as source of Vitamin C

indicators.note: to roll things is to tumble them about, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A health tip: a bread roll is a must as a vitamin source.
explanation.definitionFit: This small citrus fruit, like a mandarin, is rich in vitamin C.

clue.text: Articles in French and English and articles of a specific type may be badly informed

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
a is the English indefinite article
ware means goods of one kind, as in kitchenware

explanation.surface: A grammar point: someone who mixes up French, English and other articles may be poorly taught.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ignorant of the facts lacks knowledge, so is poorly informed.

clue.text: Resort place is distinctive

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, so the following letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An advert boasting that a holiday resort is a distinctive place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday spot but is read as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of the ordinary and unusual stands apart, which is what distinctive means.

clue.text: Similar to Stubbs (or not so)

parts.note: Una Stubbs, the British actress
similar to means like

explanation.surface: Is a painting like the work of George Stubbs, or not?
explanation.walkthrough: Stubbs suggests George Stubbs the horse painter, but it is Una Stubbs, a British TV actress; resembling Una is Una-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Different things are not similar, so 'not so' denies the likeness stated just before.

clue.text: Lumberjack's exit?

parts.note: a timber cutter's departure would be taking timber away, the same phrase used for ending a computer session

explanation.surface: A lumberjack walking off the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Ending a computer session is described with the same words as carrying timber out of the woods.

clue.text: Drinks containing vermouth — these always leave some of you on the floor

definitions.text: these always leave some of you on the floor

indicators.note: containing says the first piece holds the second

parts.note: to sup is to drink
IT is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: Cocktails with vermouth that always leave some drinkers flat on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition seems to continue the drunkenness picture, but describes an exercise done lying on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: In these abdominal exercises the legs and lower back stay on the floor while the torso rises.

clue.text: Set out with soft footfall

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: Someone setting out quietly on soft feet.
explanation.definitionFit: The sound or act of a foot coming down is a single pace.

clue.text: Emerson missing from ELP recording

definitions.meaning: ELP is the rock band Emerson, Lake and Palmer; dropping E for Emerson leaves LP, a long-playing record
a gramophone record, or any recorded release

explanation.surface: A rock band's record made without its keyboard player Keith Emerson.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part is wordplay that lands on LP, which then stands for the answer it describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A vinyl LP is a flat round record, and a recording is issued on one.

clue.text: Extremists almost put off out of range

parts.note: ultras are extremists or fanatics

indicators.note: almost says the phrase loses its last letter

parts.note: a plan put off is put on ice

explanation.surface: Radicals nearly postponed something that was beyond reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of range' means beyond human hearing, not physical distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound above about twenty kilohertz is beyond the range of human hearing.

clue.text: Old Afrikaner farmer's no Romeo? Cor!

indicators.note: no says the letter is absent

parts.note: a Boer is an Afrikaner farmer
R is Romeo in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An exclamation at an old Afrikaner farmer who is no great lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cor!' looks like a British exclamation of surprise, but it is the cor anglais, a larger relative of the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The cor anglais is a member of the double-reed woodwind family and is the tenor relative, so it stands for it.

clue.text: Person working to learn software runs draw

parts.note: an app is a piece of software
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
to draw someone in is to entice them

explanation.surface: Software that runs a lottery draw.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee learns a trade on the job, working while being taught.
